howToRefresh: Ingest the KY History morning email to public/content/raw-briefs/YYYY-MM-DD.md, run npm run parse-briefs, then npm run build (includes build-home-preview). The homepage also re-reads stories.json in the browser.

stories.title: Jack Jouett, Kentucky’s midnight rider
stories.summary: On the night of June 3–4, 1781, Capt. John “Jack” Jouett spotted Banastre Tarleton’s British cavalry near Cuckoo Tavern in Virginia and rode roughly forty miles over back roads…
stories.quote: On the night of June 3–4, 1781, Capt. John “Jack” Jouett spotted Banastre Tarleton’s British cavalry near Cuckoo Tavern in Virginia and rode roughly forty miles over back roads to warn Thomas Jefferson at Monticello and the Virginia Assembly at Charlottesville.

stories.title: Chickamauga Cherokee hold the southern flank
stories.summary: After the 1775 Treaty of Sycamore Shoals sold Cherokee claims to Kentucky hunting ground, Dragging Canoe (Tsiyu Gansini) broke with the accommodationist chiefs, warning of a…
stories.quote: After the 1775 Treaty of Sycamore Shoals sold Cherokee claims to Kentucky hunting ground, Dragging Canoe (Tsiyu Gansini) broke with the accommodationist chiefs, warning of a “dark and bloody ground.” From new towns on Chickamauga Creek (and later the Five Lower Towns), his Chickamauga faction — Cherokees plus allied Creek, Shawnee, and others — raided Cumberland and Kentucky settlements through the Revolution and into the 1790s.

layers.blurb: A Pleistocene salt lick where mastodons left bones in the mud — Kentucky’s window on deep time.

layers.name: Old Talbott Tavern
layers.blurb: Court Square tavern since the late 1700s — among America’s oldest inns, still a working bourbon bar.

layers.name: Goddard Covered Bridge
layers.blurb: White Bridge: a Town-lattice span over Sand Lick Creek, among Kentucky’s surviving covered bridges.

layers.name: Bourbon Iron Works
layers.blurb: Jacob Myers blew in a charcoal blast furnace here in 1791 — munitions for the early Commonwealth.

layers.name: The Kentucke Gazette

layers.name: Cumberland Falls
layers.blurb: The “Niagara of the South,” and one of the few Western Hemisphere places a moonbow can appear.

layers.name: Frankfort Cemetery
layers.blurb: Hilltop rural cemetery (1844) overlooking the capital — Daniel and Rebecca Boone were reinterred here.
